classification.difficultyReason: Follow the specified coefficient comparison, pairing complementary powers from the two factors and recognising their sum in the combined expansion.

content.prompt:
By considering $(1+x)^n(1+x)^{2m}=(1+x)^{n+2m}$, equate the coefficient of $x^k$ to show that
$$\binom nk\binom{2m}0+\binom n{k-1}\binom{2m}1+\binom n{k-2}\binom{2m}2+\cdots$$
is equal to $\displaystyle\binom{n+2m}k$.

answer.worked:
In the product, choose $x^{k-j}$ from the first factor and $x^j$ from the second. Each contributes $\binom n{k-j}\binom{2m}j$ to the coefficient of $x^k$.

The coefficient of $x^k$ in $(1+x)^{n+2m}$ is $\binom{n+2m}k$. Equating coefficients gives
$$\begin{align*}
\binom nk\binom{2m}0+\binom n{k-1}\binom{2m}1+\binom n{k-2}\binom{2m}2+\cdots
&=\binom{n+2m}k.
\end{align*}$$
Only terms whose lower indices lie within the corresponding expansion occur.
